topics: next steps: canary and artifacts exchange
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-28 14:00 UTC — Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE) — Daniel Park (LucidPath CTO), Sana Rodriguez (ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Infra), Ethan Lim (Product)

Auto-summary: Redwood presented bench CSV and latency histograms; discussed p95 improvements and tuning steps. Action items captured.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we ran the full head-to-head last night and have the trimmed results to walk through, hope that's still good timing for you
00:12 Daniel Park: yeah good thanks maya, excited to see numbers — been eager to know where the delta actually is versus our incumbent (MegaVendor AI)
00:22 Liam O'Neill: quick note, we used the same request mix you gave us in the traffic profile doc, ran 30 minute sustained runs plus a few 5 minute spikes to 20% higher load, and then isolated cold start runs for the p99 tails
00:40 Sana Rodriguez: when you say "isolated cold", do you mean kernel cold or KV cache cold? those matter a lot for our long session flows
00:48 Liam O'Neill: good call, so we did both — kernel cold for container spin-up and KV cache cold where the KV was purged before the run, so you get both behaviors in the CSV
01:02 Priya Kapoor: slight transcription lag on my end but i can follow — curious about the absolute numbers though, what did p95 look like?
01:10 Arjun Patel: here's the headline: Redwood p95 median across runs was ~120ms for 256-token average sequences, incumbent p95 was ~200ms. p50 was 60ms vs 95ms. throughput peak sustainable was 450 RPS on Redwood vs 320 RPS incumbent under same hardware/instance class.
01:36 Ethan Lim: wow that's a noticeable improvement — is that with quantized models or full fp16?
01:42 Liam O'Neill: these runs used our int8-ish quant profile (we call it q8-approx) but we also included a fp16 control. int8 gave ~1.6x throughput improvement with less than 1.5% QA delta on your eval prompts. fp16 p95 was around 160ms in our control runs, so quant helped but not the whole story — continuous batching and KV prefix reuse also cut token overhead
02:06 Daniel Park: any chance that the numbers are optimistic because of warm caches? our production will have many cold sessions early in a day
02:14 Liam O'Neill: yes the cold-starts are higher — in the cold-run CSV p95 jumped to ~380ms for the first request but after warmup it settles. part of our playbook is short-lived pre-warm bursts and routing to warm pools for critical flows, we can show fallback routing too
02:33 Sana Rodriguez: did you capture tail histograms? p99/p999?
02:38 Arjun Patel: p99 for warm runs was ~340ms for Redwood, incumbent p99 ~720ms. p999 on short runs was noisy but Redwood still trended lower. we'll attach the histograms (see shared: drive.google.com/lucidpath/pilot-results.csv)
03:00 Priya Kapoor: we need to reconcile instance types — did you use the same GPUs as our incumbent benchmark or approximate?
03:07 Liam O'Neill: we matched the instance family where possible, NV48-ish class; small differences in driver sets might exist. Priya, we'll include the exact AMI/driver/container sha in the CSV so you can map 1:1
03:20 Daniel Park: unit cost? i know you said per-token similar, do you have a ballpark for requests per second to $/1k tokens
03:28 Maya Chen: rough numbers from the run: under the pilot traffic our unit cost projection is ~0.8x of incumbent when using q8 profiles and Redwood batching. That's before reserved slot discounts. we'll send a pricing sketch
03:45 Ethan Lim: about accuracy — you said 1.5% delta on your eval prompts, were those the same prompts we provided in the sample set?
03:52 Liam O'Neill: yes we used your sample prompts and your eval harness. some corner cases showed higher delta (rare hallucination on long-form summarization) — we flagged those and have a prompt/temperature tuning suggestion
04:12 Sana Rodriguez: hm, we need to see the prompt-level diffs. can you show one or two examples now?
04:18 Arjun Patel: sure — Example A: incumbent trimmed content oddly on bullet 3, Redwood preserved structure but added a small extra line — we annotated these in the results sheet. Example B: long context summarization had a 0.8 BLEU drop but human reviewers still preferred Redwood output in 3/5 samples
04:46 Daniel Park: operational question — our security team will want to know about audit logs and KMS integration if we go private. any blockers?
04:54 Maya Chen: no blockers — our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS, audit log export, and SSO/SAML. for the POC we ran on Hosted with encrypted volumes but we can spin up a Private trial if needed
05:10 Priya Kapoor: that's great. timeline wise, if we want a canary on dedicated slots how quickly can you provision?
05:16 Maya Chen: we can provision a dedicated slot within 48 hours depending on capacity; if you want a guaranteed window we'll reserve it once we confirm the billing/commitment sketch
05:28 Daniel Park: ok let's plan for a 2-hour canary next week during our low traffic window. Priya will confirm the exact day.
05:36 Priya Kapoor: i'll check and get back in slack by EOD tomorrow
05:40 Liam O'Neill: technical caveat — for the canary we'll want to run two scenarios: sustained 30-minute ramp and then a 2x spike for 10 minutes to exercise autoscaling and fallback. also validate prefix KV behavior across restarts
06:00 Sana Rodriguez: curious about the routing: you talked about model variants and fallback to a cheaper model. does that affect latency SLOs?
06:08 Arjun Patel: yes it can. our routing policy is SLO-first: if latency rises beyond threshold we route to a compatible lower-cost variant that has slightly higher perplexity but maintains response time. we keep response quality metrics in the console so you can set alerts
06:28 Daniel Park: what about our regulatory need for data residency in eu-west-1?
06:32 Maya Chen: we have region pinning and can run Private control planes in your VPCs in eu-west-1. for the Hosted POC, we used eu-west-1 infra for these runs to match your residency requirement
06:45 Ethan Lim: any surprises in the logs? we saw a couple of spikes in p95 during the 20% load tests — cause known?
06:52 Liam O'Neill: spikes traced to occasional GC pauses in the older runtime we used for the incumbent; in our stack we tuned kernel threads and batching windows to reduce GC impact. a few driver mismatches caused small outliers; we'll annotate them in the trace export
07:20 Daniel Park: that makes sense. are there any potential regressions we should be worried about if we go all-in?
07:26 Maya Chen: the known tradeoffs are quantization accuracy in a few long-form tasks and slightly higher cold-start p95s if you don't use warm pools. both are addressable: we can offer a canary with warm pool enabled and a rollback to fp16 if needed
07:42 Priya Kapoor: sounds reasonable. can we get the raw traces and the exact container sha so our infra team can reproduce?
07:47 Arjun Patel: yes, we'll drop the traces in the shared folder and include container sha, AMI, nvidia-driver version, and the benchmark script commit hash
08:06 Sana Rodriguez: one more thing — how will you measure inference cost for our mixed workload? tokens are one part; model context length and prompt prep matter too
08:16 Liam O'Neill: agreed, so we provided per-request token breakdown plus an average context multiply column in the CSV. we'll also include a cost-per-1000-requests row using your workload mix
08:36 Maya Chen: recap and next steps: Redwood to share trimmed CSV, histograms, trace bundle, and pricing sketch by 2026-09-01. LucidPath to share production traces and confirm canary window by 2026-09-02. Book dedicated slot once both sides confirm.
08:58 Daniel Park: thanks all, appreciate the transparency. i'll loop in legal/security if we move to Private trial.
09:06 Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and post artifacts to the shared drive.

End of transcript.

References and artifacts shared during call: drive.google.com/lucidpath/pilot-results.csv ; deck: drive.google.com/lucidpath/pilot-deck-v2.pdf ; internal: /confluence/lucidpath/poc-notes (note: link restricted)
